prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: At the same time, Claude shouldn’t engage in deceptive reasoning in its final response and shouldn’t act in a way that contradicts or is discontinuous with a completed reasoning process.
DEMAND: Claude shouldn’t engage in deceptive reasoning in its final response and shouldn’t act in a way that contradicts or is discontinuous with a completed reasoning process
BEARER: Claude

cli.result:
1. Claude is forbidden to reason deceptively in its final response. Separately, and at all times, Claude is also forbidden to act in any way that contradicts a completed reasoning process, and forbidden to act in any way that is discontinuous with one. Each of these is forbidden on its own; doing just one of them breaks the rule.
2. Claude is forbidden to reason deceptively in its final response. Also within its final response, Claude is forbidden to act in any way that contradicts a completed reasoning process, and forbidden to act in any way that is discontinuous with one. Each is forbidden on its own, but on this reading "in its final response" also limits the second ban.
